solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Standard car coat

parts.note: par = the standard or norm
the Ford Ka, a small car

explanation.surface: A no-frills coat for wearing in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a 'car coat' being a real short coat; split it after 'car' and the last word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the parka, a hooded anorak, is one kind of coat.

clue.text: Clergyman bored by the author's unknown meanness

indicators.note: the clergyman has a hole drilled in him, with the next piece put inside

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman
the author's = the setter is = I'M
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A stingy vicar whose meanness has the author puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the author' means the person who wrote the clue, so 'the author's' stands for 'I am', contracted. The clergyman is bored as with a drill, and those letters fill the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme unwillingness to spend, meanness.

clue.text: French wine: dissolute type drinking gallons

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: A libertine knocking back French wine by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: The roué drinking by the gallon is the picture, and the verb is the container instruction too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is French for red, so vin rouge is red wine.

clue.text: War hero in Far East regularly catching cold

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within 'Far East'
the letters hold the next piece inside
something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at an even spacing, every second one

parts.note: every second letter of fAr EaSt
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A soldier out in the Far East who keeps going down with colds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Far East is not a place here, just the letters that are picked from. Achilles fought in the Trojan War, far from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek hero of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Record numbers peer at back of tower

indicators.note: the peer is placed after the tower

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
a count is a nobleman, a peer

explanation.surface: A nobleman at the back of a tower, counting heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to look closely, but it is a noun: a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to keep count of something is to record the numbers as they mount up.

clue.text: Decisive punch, extremely harmful, is cause of black eye

parts.note: KO = knockout

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters of HarmfuL

explanation.surface: A knockout blow, harmful indeed, leaving the victim with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a boxing injury; the 'black eye' is really one made up with cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is a black powder used to darken the eyelids, so it gives a black eye of a kind.

clue.text: In hairy situation finally get in a rage

parts.note: finally = in the end
to get angered is to get in a rage

explanation.surface: Someone in a tight spot who finally loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' is informal for dangerous or frightening, so a hairy situation is a perilous one.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hairy' is informal for dangerous, so a hairy situation is one of danger, and being in it is being endangered.

clue.text: Revolution supported by what may offer entitlement

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power
on = resting on, held up by

explanation.surface: A revolution backed by those who feel entitled to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supported by' does double duty: it places COUP above, and gives ON itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon entitles its holder to a discount or a free item.

clue.text: Tea turned out to be free of additives

indicators.note: the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Tea that has turned out to be pure, with nothing added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the indicator, but it is part of the fodder; 'out' alone shuffles TEA TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untreated has had nothing added to it or done to it.

clue.text: Almost broken chain is light to carry

parts.note: TORN without its last letter
CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A snapped chain that has become light enough to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as not heavy; it is the noun, a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: the British torch is what Americans call a flashlight, carried in the hand.

clue.text: Hasty notes about using non-slip footwear

parts.note: rough = hasty, as in a rough sketch

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the notes are read backwards

parts.note: doh is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone scribbling quick notes about grippy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Roughshod horseshoes had projecting nails to stop slipping, hence the phrase 'ride roughshod'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughshod horse wears shoes with nails left sticking out for grip.

clue.text: Complete lunatic, off his head

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: NUTTER without its first letter N

explanation.surface: Describing someone as a total madman, out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off his head' is slang for mad, which suits a lunatic, but here it tells you to behead him. A nutter is British slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the intensifying sense: an utter fool is a complete fool.

clue.text: I give a hand, at the outset specifying highest standards

indicators.note: take the start of the next word

parts.note: used as it stands
to deal is to hand out the cards for a hand
first letter of Specifying

explanation.surface: A helper who insists from the start on the very best standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a hand' suggests help, but it is the card player's hand, which is dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ideals are standards of perfection, the ones set highest.

clue.text: Chief not involved in modern industry

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A boss who keeps out of the running of a modern business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not involved' reads as a phrase meaning detached; the indicator is 'involved' alone, and 'not' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: information technology is one of the newer industries.

clue.text: Official publication I run in government

parts.note: mag = magazine
used as it stands
the state = the government
R = run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An official publication claiming that I run the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official publication' reads as one thing, a government paper, but 'Official' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a public official who administers the law.

clue.text: What reduces exposure to UV round area better?

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is an area
a better is one who bets, which a layer does too: to lay a bet

explanation.surface: Asking what would cut down on sunburn round here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as the comparative, but it is one who bets; a layer lays odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere absorbs most ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

clue.text: Wildly revelling, so tragic I collapsed

indicators.note: the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Partying so hard that it ends in a tragic collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The collapse fits the party, and it is also the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic means marked by wild revelry.

clue.text: Above patronising theatre performance

parts.note: at = attending, as a patron of a shop is at it
an op, an operation, is performed in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Looking down on a theatre show with a superior air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronising' suggests condescension; here it means frequenting, being at. The theatre is the surgeon's, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hat atop the head sits on top of it.

clue.text: Popular stop where almost everyone gets on

indicators.note: almost everyone is not quite all, so the word stops one letter short
boards, gets into, the word for stop

parts.note: to prevent is to stop
ALL without its last letter
surface padding: sets the scene at the stop

explanation.surface: A busy bus stop where nearly everybody climbs aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a bus stop; 'stop' is the verb, and 'gets on' means boards, going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevalent means widespread, generally found, popular in that sense.

clue.text: They fly in for summer having entered a race from far away

indicators.note: A has gone inside the birds

parts.note: house martins are birds that migrate to Britain for the summer
used as it stands

explanation.surface: Visitors who fly in for the summer season to join a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads like holidaymakers; it describes martins, summer visitors from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Martians are the imagined race from Mars, far away indeed.

clue.text: In the past year turned to a system of exercises

indicators.note: the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: ago = in the past
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone who took up exercising in the last year.
explanation.walkthrough: AGO and Y join to make AGOY, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the postures of hatha yoga form a set routine of exercises.

clue.text: Diesel adds different way to experience horse-power

indicators.note: the letters are made into something different

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Diesel offering another way to get horsepower out of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse-power is engine talk in the surface; the definition means riding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle, both legs on one side, is one way to be carried by a horse.

clue.text: Painter perhaps turned into almost complete artist

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way
almost complete is not quite whole, so the word stops one letter short

parts.note: WHOLE without its last letter

indicators.note: goes inside the next piece

parts.note: RA = Royal Academician, a painter for example

explanation.surface: A painter who has turned himself into a nearly complete artist.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the crossword's usual painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist.

clue.text: Bread agency delivered pancake mixture

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: as a speech is delivered: spoken

parts.note: batter is the mixture pancakes are made from

explanation.surface: A bakery firm that delivers pancake mix along with its loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a van round, but it means spoken, as a speech is delivered. In a non-rhotic British accent BATTER and the end of CIABATTA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ciabatta is one Italian bread among many.

clue.text: Copper base raised somewhat

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bed is a base, as a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: A copper foundation that has been lifted a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised somewhat' sounds like lifted a little; a number cubed is raised to the third power.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubed means raised to the power of three, which is raising a number somewhat.

clue.text: Woman's appeal about to make an impact

indicators.note: the appeal goes around the next piece

parts.note: SA = sex appeal
to tell is to have an effect, as in 'the strain began to tell'

explanation.surface: A woman's charm about to make its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the name to the wordplay. 'About' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stella is one of many women's names.

clue.text: Ill-gotten gains Hercules stores up

indicators.note: the name keeps the answer inside it
in a down clue, read the letters upwards

parts.note: hERCULes read backwards

explanation.surface: A strongman hoarding his loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercules could be a real hoarder in the surface, but his name only holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in 'filthy lucre', is money gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Vegetable for example not used in keg beer

parts.words: for example not used in keg
parts.note: KEG without EG, the abbreviation for 'for example'
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A vegetable that is never used when brewing keg beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' reads as introducing an instance; it is EG, removed from KEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: kale is one of the cabbage family of vegetables.

clue.text: Tough only child

parts.note: but = only, as in 'but a child'
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: An only child who has to be tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only child' is a fixed phrase, but 'only' and 'child' give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch means tough and aggressively masculine.

clue.text: A piece of drapery cushioning husband's heavy fall

parts.note: used as it stands
a valance is a short curtain or frill of drapery
H = husband

explanation.surface: A curtain breaking a husband's hard fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The husband's fall is cushioned by drapery in the surface; the 'heavy fall' is of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an avalanche is snow or rock coming down a mountainside in great mass.

clue.text: Officer in scrap cut just above the chest

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the word for scrap

parts.note: to scrap text is to delete it
Col = Colonel

explanation.surface: An officer wounded in a fight, cut just above the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, and 'cut' a wound; the scrap is the verb, delete, and the cut is of a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A décolleté dress is cut low, leaving the neck and shoulders bare down to just above the chest.

clue.text: Exhausted writer nursed by good man

indicators.note: the writer is held inside, as a baby is nursed

parts.note: ST = saint, a good man
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: A worn-out author being looked after by a kind man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the pen. A saint as 'good man' gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spent runner, like a spent force, has nothing left.
